attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use comments to create multiple sections in the editor to better organize your code?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What code might be placed underneath each comment?

❓ How do you create blank lines in the JavaScript editor?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Explain to the ninja that typing // tells the project to skip over the text that follows and move onto the next line of code. Just as when naming sprites, it’s useful to be short and descriptive when writing comments.
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by adding code comments to organize where the code will go in the editor!


Add comments with these descriptions to the project: project set up, array set up, display usernames.


Start each comment with // and add several blank lines between each comment.

steps.hints: ❓ Does each variable name match the question asked in each askForString function?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What topics might you ask the user about?

❓ What short and descriptive names might you use for each variable that match the question asked?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Offer the ninja a few suggestions of topics to ask the user about. Suggestions include: the user’s favorite food, color, clothing, friend, snack, movie, etc.

💡 Remind the ninja to update the answerLength accordingly in each askForString, so that the user has enough characters to complete their string.
steps.instructions:
Ask the user to share a few of their favorite things!


Declare a new variable called favAnimal underneath // array set up. Open Game and drag [ask for string (message)] to the right of the assignment operator. Replace null with a string that asks the user what their favorite animal is. Update the answerLength parameter to set how long the user’s response can be. Then, add a blank line below the favAnimal variable declaration. 


Repeat these steps to declare 3 additional variables below the first one, asking the user to submit strings sharing 3 more of their favorite things. Leave a blank line between each variable declaration. 


Click ▶ to see the project ask the user to share a string about 4 of their favorite things!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add the push function to the empty string array name under each variable’s declaration?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What does the push function do? How is it used?

❓ Why might it be useful to write a comment telling the index value of each element in the words array?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 In JavaScript, the push function adds an element to the end of an array. In this example, the values of the 4 string variables are being added to the end of the words array.

💡 Remind the ninja that the index of elements in an array begin at 0 and increase by 1 with each element added.

💡 Later in this project, the ninja will use the user-submitted strings in a nested array to form username suggestions. For this reason, it will be useful to quickly find the index value of each element.

💡Make sure the Ninja has used the correct syntax to set up the words array to pass validation. There should be a space between the colon and the array type and the string data type should use a lowercase “s”. The code should look like: 

let words: string[] = []
steps.instructions:
Push user-submitted strings to an empty array!


Use the keyword let to declare an empty string array called words underneath // project set up. Type a colon, the array type, and a pair of brackets: : string[]. Then, add an assignment operator and a second pair of brackets [ ]. 


Use the push function to add the user-submitted strings to the words array. On the blank line below the favAnimal variable code, type the name of the array followed by a dot operator. Select push from the code completion tool, then add a pair of parentheses with the favAnimal variable name typed inside. After the parentheses, type the comment // index 0 as a reminder that the favAnimal variable will be stored at index 0 in the words array.


Repeat these steps to push the values of the other 3 variables to the words array on the blank line below each variable declaration. Use a comment to show the index value that each element will be stored at, which will increase by 1 with each new element added.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you edit the string and answerLength parameters of the askForNumber function to customize the question and set how long the user’s response can be?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What topics might you ask the user about?

❓ What short and descriptive names might you use for each variable that match the question asked?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Offer the ninja a few suggestions of topics to ask the user about. Suggestions include: the user’s lucky number, the day of their birthday, their age, etc. 

💡Point out to the ninja that while it’s okay to use “favorite numbers” in a MakeCode project, they should not offer sensitive information to strangers.

💡 Remind the ninja to update the answerLength parameter accordingly in each askForNumber, so that the user has enough characters to complete their number.
steps.instructions:
Ask the user to share a few of their favorite numbers!


Declare a new variable called birthdayMonth underneath the 4 string variables under // array set up. Open Game and drag [ask for number (message)] to the right of the assignment operator. Replace null with a string that asks the user what month their birthday is in. Use 2 as the answerLength parameter.


Repeat these steps to declare 2 additional variables below the birthdayMonth variable, asking the user to share 2 more of their favorite numbers. Leave a blank line between each variable declaration. 


Click ▶ to see the project ask the user to share 3 of their favorite numbers!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type the names of each variable inside the parentheses of the push function?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why do you think an error message appears when the number variables are pushed to the words array?

❓ What does the push function do? How is it used?

❓ Why might it be useful to write a comment telling the index value of each element in the words array?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 In JavaScript, the push function adds an element to the end of an array. In this example, the values of the 3 number variables are being added to the end of the words array.

💡 Remind the ninja that the index of elements in an array begin at 0 and increase by 1 with each element added. The number variables should begin at index 4.

💡 Later in this project, the ninja will use the user-submitted strings in a nested array to form username suggestions. For this reason, it will be useful to quickly find the matching index value for each element.
steps.instructions:
Push user-submitted numbers to the array!


Use the push function to add the user-submitted numbers to the words array. On the line below the birthdayMonth variable code, type the name of the array followed by a dot operator. 


Select push from the code completion tool, then type a pair of parentheses with the name of the birthdayMonth variable inside. Add the comment // index 4 as a reminder that the birthdayMonth variable will be stored at index 4 in the words array.


Repeat these steps to push the values of the other 2 number variables to the words array on the blank line below each variable declaration. Use a comment to show the index value that each element will be stored at, which will increase by 1 with each new element added.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the toString function after each number variable’s name inside the parentheses of the push function?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why does the value of each number variable need to be converted to a string, in order to be added to the words array?

❓ What does the toString function do? How is it used?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Explain to the ninja that the words array can only contain string values. In each of the number variables, the askForNumber function stores a number value submitted by the user. Because arrays can only store the same type of element, the number values are unable to be pushed to the words array in their current form.

💡 In JavaScript, the toString function returns a string representation of a number. This function converts the number value into a string value, and consequently, the values stored in the number variables are able to be pushed to the words array.
steps.instructions:
Oh no! An error message appears when the number values are pushed to the words array.


Notice that the number variables store number values, but the words array can only contain string values. The number variables will need to be converted to string values before they can be pushed to the words array.


Inside the parentheses of the birthdayMonth variable’s push code, type a dot operator after birthdayMonth, then select toString from the code completion tool. The toString function will return a string representation of the number. After, type a pair of parentheses so the code looks like:

words.push(birthdayMonth.toString())

Repeat these steps to add the toString function to the push code of the other 2 number variables.


Now, each time a user submits a favorite number, it will be added to the words array as a string value.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you create a new array, then add elements using the index values of the words array?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What might the elements in the userName array be used for?

❓ Which index values might you join together to create a unique username? Why?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Explain to the ninja that the 3 elements at the index values of the words array will be added to the userName array. In the next step, these 3 elements will be combined to form a username suggestion for the user. Encourage the ninja to use a combination of string and number values to create a unique username.

💡 Encourage the ninja to look back at the different variables they’ve created in order to select 3 that might go together to form a username. Point out to the ninja that they should use the code comments to quickly identify the index value that each variable is stored at.

💡 Double check that the ninja has included brackets to include all 3 elements of the array, brackets to retrieve each index’s value from the words array, and have used a comma to separate each element.
steps.instructions:
Combine the user-submitted strings and numbers to form a username!


Create a new array called userName underneath the existing code under // array set up. Type a pair of brackets [ ] to set up the array. Inside the brackets, type words followed by another pair of brackets [ ], with the number 2 typed inside. Now, the value at index 2 of the words array will be added to the userName array. 


Type a comma, then add another value to the userName array by typing words[ ]. Type a different number between 0-6 inside the brackets to indicate the index value of the element that will be added to the userName array. Repeat this step to add a third element from the words array to the userName array.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the join function to combine the values from the userName array?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What message will appear when the showLongText code runs?

❓ What does the join function do? How is it similar to concatenating values using a plus sign +?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When the showLongText code runs, a dialog box will appear that says “Username option:” and the 3 values from userName combined, with no spaces between them.

💡 Previously, the ninja has used a plus sign + to concatenate values together. The join function works similarly; it joins all the elements of an array into a single string value. The string separator parameter sets what will be placed between each value. In this case, since the username suggestion should be 1 consecutive word, there should be no spaces between each value.
steps.instructions:
Share a username suggestion based on the user’s submitted strings and numbers!


Open Game and drag [show long text (str) (layout)] underneath // display usernames. Replace null with a string that says:


“Username option: “


Then, use + to concatenate the string with the elements in the userName array. 


Type the name of the array followed by a dot operator, then select the join function from the code completion tool. The join function will join all elements of an array into a string. After join, type a pair of parentheses with quotation marks without any space between them inside. This will set the string separator parameter to join each value from the array without any spaces in between.


Be sure to update the layout parameter, too.


Click ▶ to see a dialog box appear with a username suggestion!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you create a nested array by adding a set of brackets [ ] around the existing values, then duplicating the inner arrays to add the second and third array of elements?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which index values might you join together to create a username?

❓ Which array of elements is at index 0 of the userName array? Index 1 and 2?

❓ Is each array of elements in the userName array surrounded by its own pair of brackets? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Point out to the ninja that since there are only 7 variable values, they can reuse 1 or more index values to create unique username suggestions.

💡 Explain to the ninja how the 3 arrays of elements are nested inside of the userName array. Index 0 of userName contains the first array of elements. Index 1 of userName contains the second array of elements. Index 2 of userName contains the third array of elements. Each value is drawn from a specific index in the words array.

💡 Double check that the ninja has included the correct number of brackets and commas in the right places.
steps.instructions:
Add additional username suggestions using a nested array!


To the right of the userName array’s assignment operator, type an opening bracket [ before the existing values. Then, press Enter to move the array of values to the line below. Type a comma to the right of the closing bracket of the first array to add additional arrays to the the userName array.


Copy (Ctrl + C) the code from the first array of elements, then paste (Ctrl + V) it on the line below. Replace the index values inside the brackets with different numbers between 0-6, to combine different elements from the words array in a new array. Type a comma to the right of the closing bracket of the second array. 


Repeat this process to create a third array within the userName array. Replace the index values inside the brackets with different numbers between 0-6. Press Enter after the closing bracket of the third array, then type a closing bracket ] on the line below it. 


Now, the userName array contains 3 nested arrays, each with 3 different elements from words within them!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you replace the index value retrieved from the userName array with the loop’s counter variable, so that a different username suggestion appears in each dialog box?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What message will appear when the showLongText code runs?

❓ What value will be pulled from the userName array each time the for loop runs?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Walk the ninja through the showLongText code. A message will appear telling the username option number, which will increase as the for loop runs. Since the for loop will run 3 times and 1 is added to the counter variable, username options 1, 2, and 3 will be displayed in the dialog box.

💡 As the for loop runs, the index value that matches the value of the counter variable i will be pulled from the userName array. Remind the ninja that each element in the userName array actually contains 3 different values. With the use of the join function, these values will be combined and displayed on the screen as a username option.
steps.instructions:
Use a loop to display the 3 different username suggestions!


Open Loops and drag [for] underneath // display usernames. Update the run condition expression by replacing 5 with the length of the userName array. Now, the for loop will begin running at 0 and continue running while the counter variable is less than the length of the userName array, for a total of 3 times.


Cut (Ctrl + X) and paste (Ctrl + V) the showLongText code inside the curly brackets of the for loop. Separate the colon from the existing string so the code looks like: 


“Username option ” + “:”

Between the strings, type (i + 1). Use another + to concatenate the colon string “:”. Now, the dialog box will show the username option starting at 1 then increasing by 1 each time the loop runs.


Add a pair of brackets after the userName array, with the counter variable i typed inside so the dialog box will show the element of userName at the index that matches the value of the counter variable. The code should look like: 


"Username option " + (i + 1) + ": " + userName[i].join("")


Click ▶ to see 3 dialog boxes appear on screen sharing different username suggestions!

steps.hints: ❓ What directions would help users understand how the project works?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What sound effect might you use to indicate the end of the project?

❓ What background color might you use as a backdrop for the project?

❓ What directions might tell the user how to play the game? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that they can delete .baDing from the music.play code, retype the dot operator, then select a new sound from the code completion tool.

💡 Remind the ninja that they can always click on the palette for one of the images in the code to open the editor. Once opened, they can hover their cursor over each individual color to find the corresponding value to use as a background color.

💡 Remind the ninja that strings need to be placed inside of quotation marks and that parameters need to be separated by a comma, otherwise the code will not be able to run correctly.
steps.instructions:
Set up how the project begins and ends!


Open Music and drag [play (toPlay) (playbackMode)] underneath // display usernames, below the for loop. Select a sound to play before the project resets. Then, open Game and drag [reset game] underneath the music.play code. 


Open Scene, drag [set background color to (color)] below the empty array code under // project set up. Set a color parameter using a number 1-15.


Open Game and drag [set dialog frame to (frame)] underneath the setBackgroundColor code. Select an image from the gallery to use as the dialog frame. Then, open Game and drag [show long text (str) (layout)] underneath the setDialogFrame code. Update the string and layout parameters, to share directions with the user.


Click ▶ to see the completed project!

subgroups.title: Username Generator
subgroups.introduction: Create a project that uses user input and nested arrays to generate username suggestions.

validationItems.text: Use the askForString function to store at least 4 user string responses.
Push the user’s string responses into a words array. Use code comments to indicate what index each element is stored at.
Use the askForNumber function to store at least 3 user number responses.
Push the user’s number responses into the words array by converting them to strings.
Combine the user’s responses in a userName array.
Use a for loop and the join function to display the user names.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about arrays and array functions. You’ll build on your understanding of arrays in JavaScript by exploring functions that will help you access, modify, and join elements in an array. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Push It, Pop It, Join It, Concat It!
badges.description: Use several different array functions in JavaScript to access and modify the data stored inside an array.

badges.title: A String of Numbers
badges.description: Use the toString function to convert a number to a string

badges.title: Arrays All The Way Down
badges.description: Create a nested array in JavaScript.

badges.title: Joined at the Hip
badges.description: Use the join function to join all the elements of a string array into one string value.

badges.title: Together Forever
badges.description: Use the concat function to join two arrays together into one new array.

badges.title: Pop It Like It’s Hot
badges.description: Use the pop function to remove and return the last element from an array.

badges.title: Group Project
badges.description: Use the allOfKind function to create an array of all sprites of the specified sprite kind.
